title: NR-RRC: lookup UE identifier from MAC,RLC,PDCP instead of MAC only
description:
In [srsRAN Project](https://github.com/srsran/srsRAN_Project), we currently add the option to save RLC-NR PDUs using UDP framing.
Like the (already present) recording of MAC-NR PDUs, this allows users a convenient inspection of 5G-NR communication.

Saving the PCAP at RLC rather than MAC allows for selective filtering of signaling radio bearers (SRBs) and data radio bearers (DRBs).
For example, the user might be interested to only save SRBs without the huge amounts of data flowing through DRBs.

In case both, SRBs and DRBs, are present in the PCAP, Wireshark should be able to derive the PDCP configuration (e.g. the sequence number length) of DRBs from the signaled values via RRC in the same way as for PCAPs at MAC layer.

However, the current NR-RRC implementation performs a look-up of the corresponding UE identifier from the MAC layer, which fails for RLC PCAPs.
With this MR, the RRC picks the UE identifier from ~~the RLC~~ MAC,RLC,PDCP (in that order), which ~~is present~~ works for both cases (MAC PCAPs and RLC PCAPs).

Example PCAPs:
- [gnb_rlc.pcap](/uploads/5103627ad5c79ccbbc7cbdb145b9eae6/gnb_rlc.pcap)
- [gnb_mac.pcap](/uploads/e73e16e801396fb97261d434a8d378d5/gnb_mac.pcap)

From the attached examples, only with the MAC PCAP current Wireshark is able to automatically determine the 18-bit SN size of PDCP layer (and continues dissection up to the TCP layer on the DRB). For the RLC PCAP, one has to manually set the PDCP SN size to 18 bit.

With the changes in this MR, it also works automatically for both PCAPs.

notes.body:
I am not against this change (which will need to be done in nr-rrc.cnf (and possibly some parts in packet-nr-rrc-template.c?)).

My selfish concern is that I need to be careful about how it might affect packet-catapult-dct2000.c (plus a couple of private dissectors I maintain). The DCT2000 dissector creates a mac_nr_info struct with the ueid field set, and calls set_mac_nr_proto_data() for LTE(for NSA)/NR RRC frames that may be logged separately (so that configuration from the functions you changed will know which ueId to configure for).  If we merge this change, I guess I could change that to call the RLC version instead...

My philosophy is usually to capture/log at the MAC level if possible so that I have some context for the higher-layer frames that are present (or not present).  What happens when you log PDCP frames carrying RRC? - you probably wouldn't have the RLC-layer info in that case.. this is why I think I chose to use the mac-level struct for tagging the UEId onto RRC frames.

A compromise might be to create and use a helper function in nr-rrc that checks mac, rlc and pdcp in order when looking for a ueid?

Hi @martin.r.mathieson,

thanks for the quick reply!

> A compromise might be to create and use a helper function in nr-rrc that checks mac, rlc and pdcp in order when looking for a ueid?

I fully agree on that. It was my first thought when looking at that line, then I decided to keep the change minimalistic. But after reading this, I think it is better to add a look-up slide through mac, rlc and pdcp. (Actually, PCAP at PDCP might also become relevant soon ;-) )

> I am not against this change (which will need to be done in nr-rrc.cnf (and possibly some parts in packet-nr-rrc-template.c?)).

Does this mean, there is some automatic code synthesis involved? This is my first attempt to contribute to Wireshark, so I'm not familiar with the build system and the whole architecture. I'd very appreciate any guidance on this change in order to avoid breaking other people's work.

Yes, the ASN1-based dissectors are generated using extracted .asn files, a conformance file (nr-rrc.cnf, where some directives are added to control code generation, and as here, a way to override/extend the generated codes for certain items in the tree) and a template .c file.  See epan/dissectors/asn1/nr-rrc.  Basically, to generate packet-nr-rrc.c, you build (make or ninja) in <build-folder>/epan/dissectors/asn1/nr-rrc (then an overall build as usual).

So it might make sense to add a helper function to look for the ueid at all three levels in the template file, and call it from the overridden handlers in the conformance file.
Thanks for the explanation. I'll try to provide an updated version soon.
Done, please have look as convenient.
marked this merge request as **draft**

Please do not break the existing behavior for your own need.
You should either:
- perform the lookup with MAC, if no hit perform the lookup with RLC, and if no hit perform the lookup with PDCP, or else
- add a preference (set to MAC by default) for the layer to be used for the lookup
Thank you for the review! I changed to the first option as suggested by @martin.r.mathieson as well.

commits_data.title: nr-rrc: lookup UE ID from MAC,RLC,PDCP (in order)
commits_data.message:
nr-rrc: lookup UE ID from MAC,RLC,PDCP (in order)

This allows Wireshark to interpret PDCP config from the
signaled value when analysing PCAPs that were taken at
RLC/PDCP layer (rather than MAC layer). In these cases,
the UE IDs cannot be looked-up from MAC layer.
